findings: Distinct provider threads are proved by session_meta, not inferred from the recovery phrase or UUID clock.
The head report created a separate normal Hornhoof job after the previous known human job finished; no overlap of these two jobs. Other invisible empty-start jobs remain unverified.
Gap from previous job finish to report creation: 36294 ms.

The new first request contains the old architecture request and head report in a recovery bootstrap. This does not prove complete provider-history preservation: server earlierTalk is bounded to 20 message/text events and preface to 48 KiB.
Notebook additions change full terminal instructions but are excluded from server session-selection hash. Both startup documents contain the exact current steady instructions.
Selected model changes server runHash even when CLI default model already has the same name. Effort is excluded from runHash, but effort and full instructions enter terminal host process hash.

Typed turns inherit a prior same-subscription hash; the first later automatic turn recalculates selected-model hash. This reproduces a fresh thread decision in fixtures, but actual incident DB hashes are missing.

A latest done job with null session can mask an older resumable job. A node also drops a requested session absent from its local cwd registry. Both paths reproduce in isolation, not proved in this incident.
Current session registry contains the two target thread-to-cwd entries. Its mtime and current entries do not prove their presence before 00:28.

Task37 safe SQLite log metadata shows distinct CLI process_uuid per old/new target thread within incident window. This proves CLI process replacement in addition to new provider thread, not its initiator.
Seven relevant installed node JS modules are byte-identical to TypeScript ESM emission from source bd696b0 with node tsconfig. Complete node build commit remains unavailable.

hypotheses.name: Head report as delivery trigger
hypotheses.for: API seq14662 links from:agent and head id to report job; prior known job done 36.294s earlier; bootstrap contains report
hypotheses.against: Report delivery normally resumes the existing provider thread when session/subscription/hash match
hypotheses.missing: Actual session-selection predecessor and job.run arguments
hypotheses.verdict: Proved trigger for Hornhoof job; thread selection cause not proved

hypotheses.name: Delayed selected-model hash after typed turns
hypotheses.for: Isolated fixture reproduces fresh catch-up; actual old/new steady instructions match; card model change reported earlier
hypotheses.against: CLI model is gpt-6.1-sol in both threads; this alone neither confirms nor refutes explicit selection/default distinction
hypotheses.missing: DB hashes/subscriptions/session ids of every adjacent job; historical model availability at dispatch
hypotheses.verdict: Strong testable hypothesis, not root cause

hypotheses.name: Notebook or effort alone
hypotheses.for: Notebook grew by 918 chars, effort max recorded in new thread; host process hash includes both
hypotheses.against: Server hash excludes notebook/effort; both documents have exact same steady; nonempty session launch uses resume
hypotheses.verdict: Not sufficient alone to explain server fresh-thread selection

hypotheses.name: Latest completed null-session start
hypotheses.for: Source selects latest eligible done job even if session_id null; isolated fixture reproduces masking older thread
hypotheses.against: No such adjacent job yet exported
hypotheses.missing: All adjacent jobs including empty prompt conversation starts

hypotheses.name: Subscription/node/session registry change or resume failure
hypotheses.for: Earlier card subscription change reported; node discards unknown or wrong-cwd sessions in isolated fixture
hypotheses.against: Current registry contains both threads; this is not historical proof. Both CLI records show same cwd/provider/version.
hypotheses.missing: Per-job subscription, requested/effective session, safe launch argv and historical node registry/process metadata

hypotheses.name: Timer
hypotheses.for: Timer dispatch shares normal queue/sessionFor selection
hypotheses.against: Known report event from agent head, not timer; no timer event in saved 49-event slice
hypotheses.missing: Full adjacent jobs and untruncated card timer/history
hypotheses.verdict: Not supported as known report initiator; hidden adjacent jobs not excluded

hypotheses.name: UI reload or reconnect
hypotheses.for: Opening missing terminal can request agent.start and produce empty start
hypotheses.against: xterm term.reset only clears display; SSE/WS reconnect alone does not erase provider thread; new provider id is real
hypotheses.missing: Browser reconnect metadata and adjacent empty-start jobs
hypotheses.verdict: Display-only explanation contradicted; indirect start path remains open

hypotheses.name: Explicit reset or compaction
hypotheses.against: Phrase is Hornhoof preface, also present on old first request; role-reset route changes role skills, not provider history; no compacted/context_compacted/abort/error record in exported lifecycle
hypotheses.missing: Full relevant runtime lifecycle/launch record; absence in saved scope is not universal absence
hypotheses.verdict: No evidence that these caused the new thread

hypotheses.name: Node/server/provider process restart
hypotheses.for: Task37 SQLite metadata proves distinct CLI process identities; host hash changes and session selection can replace CLI process
hypotheses.against: Task37 ps snapshot PID1 node started23:11:00 in stated Codex container and tmux93 at23:11:02, before incident. Codex94 in that ps is not target CLI process.
hypotheses.missing: Exact process/hello/restart logs and node build for 00:28:16Z..00:28:56Z
hypotheses.verdict: CLI process replacement proved; corresponding container PID1 startup predates incident. Server/other-node restart and replacement initiator unproved.

hypotheses.name: Operations MCP no-turn error

hypotheses.against: Company turn open/closed is not checked there; no failed-call/job ids supplied
